VERDICT: ACCEPTThe two objections are resolved in the revised note. I independently checked the parity assertion and the new local closed-receiver argument. The written mathematics now supports the stated conclusions under the stated hypotheses.The scoped Lean and execution receipts are not needed for this verdict.1. The odd-start parity correction is correctFor a rail beginning at  $a_i$ , the last rail column is
$$b_i=a_i+2\ell_i-1.$$
Because  $2\ell_i-1$  is odd:if  $a_i$  is odd, then  $b_i$  is even;if  $a_i$  is even, then  $b_i$  is odd.Since  $w$  is even,  $w-1$  is odd. Therefore an odd-start rail cannot end at  $w-1$ . Its largest possible endpoint is  $w-2$ . The clipped physical tile  $\{w-1,w\}$  occurs only for an even-start rail.Thus the revised parity split is correct.For odd  $a_i$ , every receiver tile is a complete physical column pair. Each end tile has:two lower-row rail endpoints,one selected cap in the upper row,one remaining upper site, forced blank because it is adjacent to the cap.There is no lower outside site in such an end tile.For even  $a_i$ , the receiver has  $\ell_i+1$  tiles:  $\ell_i-1$  complete interior tiles and two partial end tiles. Each partial end tile has:one rail endpoint,one cap,one upper outside site, forced blank by the cap,one lower outside site.The lower outside site is blank because an interior one cannot be  $P$  by completeness and cannot be  $T$  while seeing both the rail endpoint and the underlying chamber endpoint. At the chamber boundaries, the original selected supports at  $(-1, -1)$  and  $(-1,w)$  force the corresponding lower outside sites blank.So the rail receiver counts are exactly
$$|R_i|=\ell_i+\epsilon_i,$$
where  $\epsilon_i=0$  for odd  $a_i$  and  $\epsilon_i=1$  for even  $a_i$ .The rail endpoint count is  $2\ell_i$ , hence
$$\frac{|R_i\cap P|}{2}=\ell_i.$$
If  $t_i$  is the number of selected upper sites in the interval, then
$$\lambda_i
=t_i+\ell_i-2(\ell_i+\epsilon_i)
=t_i-\ell_i-2\epsilon_i.$$
The selected upper sites form an independent set on a path of  $2\ell_i$  positions: adjacent selections would each see their own rail endpoint and the other selected site. Therefore
$$t_i\le \ell_i.$$
The old elbow receiver still contributes exactly one, so with
$$L=\sum_i(\ell_i-t_i)\ge0,
\qquad
E=\sum_i\epsilon_i\ge0,$$
the exact total charge is
$$\rho_H
=1+\sum_i\lambda_i
=1-L-2E
\le1.$$
The rigidity statement is also correct:
$$\rho_H>0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
L=0,\ E=0,$$
which means every rail starts at odd phase and carries a maximum independent set of upper selections.There is no remaining parity or boundary counterexample.2. The local closed-receiver identity is now valid without terminalityThe revised Section 3 no longer relies on the generic receiver ownership theorem from COMPONENT_RECEIVERS_AND_SQUARE_FREE_BOUND.md. Instead it proves the needed identity directly from the saturated/deficient correction. That resolves the previous scope objection, provided the saturated-tile lemma is indeed valid for every feasible pair.It is.For a physical tile  $Q$ , feasibility gives  $t_Q\le2$ . The needed stronger facts follow locally.Saturated tile with two adjacent selected sitesIf  $t_Q=2$  and the two selected sites are adjacent, any additional endpoint in the tile is adjacent to one of those selected sites while the selected sites are adjacent to each other. That selected site would then see two occupied neighbors. Hence such a tile has no endpoint.Saturated tile with opposite selected sitesIf  $t_Q=2$  and the selected sites are opposite, the two remaining corners are each adjacent to both selected sites. Consequently the tile can contain at most one endpoint:
$$p_Q\le1.$$
There is no internal matching edge in a saturated tile because an internal matching edge would require two endpoints.It remains to rule out an edge from the endpoint of a saturated tile to the endpoint of another saturated tile. If a saturated tile has one endpoint, its two selected sites are opposite and its endpoint occupies one of the remaining corners. Across any side through which that endpoint could be matched, the other saturated tile would have the corresponding opposite-selected pattern. The two nonendpoint seam vertices would then be selected in the positions facing one another across the seam. Each of those selected vertices would see:the endpoint in its own tile, andthe selected vertex across the seam.That violates feasibility. The vertical case is identical after rotation.Therefore every endpoint in a saturated tile is matched to a deficient tile, even without single-terminality.Now let  $U$  be the receiver, viewed as a union of full physical tiles, and assume every endpoint in  $U$  has its actual mate in  $U$ . In the revised geometry this closure holds because:the exhaustive receiver labels exclude foreign endpoints; $H$  is the complete endpoint component;the displayed matching is closed on  $H$ .For every saturated tile in  $U$ , its endpoint mates a deficient tile in  $U$ . Conversely, every deficient-tile correction  $s_Q/2$  corresponds to a saturated endpoint in  $U$ . Thus the matching induces a bijection between:the endpoint incidences in saturated tiles, andthe deficient-tile incidences counted by  $s_Q$ .Since a saturated tile has
$$e_Q=t_Q+\frac{p_Q}{2}-2=\frac{p_Q}{2}$$
and corrected charge zero, the sum of saturated raw excesses is exactly the sum of all deficient  $s_Q/2$  corrections. Consequently
$$\sum_{Q\subset U}\rho(Q)
=
\sum_{Q\subset U}e_Q.$$
This gives
$$\rho_H
=
|T\cap V(\operatorname{receiver})|
+\frac{|H|}{2}
-2|\operatorname{receiver}|,$$
without importing terminal ownership.The old elbow receiver labels remain fixed under arbitrary feasible exterior data. The retained supports force the nonendpoint corners blank, and completeness of  $H$  excludes foreign endpoints at corners adjacent to  $H$ . The rails lie in the separate row band  $\{-2,-1\}$ , so they do not alter any old receiver label.The only saturated old receiver tiles are the prescribed tip tiles, and their unique endpoints are matched to deficient receiver tiles inside the same closed receiver. Rail tiles are deficient because their upper selections are independent and hence at most one per physical tile. Therefore the local correction argument is complete.3. The freezing obstruction remains valid for all rails and mixed bundlesThe inherited elbow certificate freezes every chamber endpoint and its mate. For a rail  $I_i$ , the first endpoint is frozen by its cap and its chamber neighbor. Thereafter:
$$(-1,a_i),\ (-1,a_i+2),\ldots,(-1,a_i+2\ell_i-2)$$
are frozen by the chamber endpoints and the mates of preceding frozen rail endpoints.The reverse wave freezes
$$(-1,a_i+2\ell_i-1),\
(-1,a_i+2\ell_i-3),\ldots,\
(-1,a_i+1).$$
The waves are disjoint and exhaust the rail for every  $\ell_i\ge2$ . They do not depend on the parity of  $a_i$ , and their retained neighbors are distinct at every step.Because each frozen endpoint retains its mate under any admissible simultaneous promotion bundle, the induction applies to mixed bundles involving exterior components. Additional exterior occupied sites cannot invalidate the freezing witnesses; they can only add occupied neighbors. The fact that the rail intervals are separated by a blank column prevents interactions between different rails.Thus every point of  $H$  is universally frozen, and the original elbow  $H_0$  cannot be isolated by either single promotions or mixed promotion bundles.4. The cross-component non-reuse ledger is correctSection 4 explicitly assumes a terminal configuration whose other components have nonpositive whole charge. Under those hypotheses, the ledger is valid.For each elbow component  $i$ ,
$$\rho_i=1-L_i-2E_i.$$
The capped-corner donor satisfies
$$d_{Q_i}\ge1.$$
The unique-owner lemma makes the chosen  $Q_i$  distinct across different endpoint components. Writing  $Z\ge0$  for the negative of the sum of the other component charges, the receiver identity gives
$$\Delta
=
\sum_{\text{unchosen no-}P\ Q}d_Q
+\sum_i(d_{Q_i}-1)
+\sum_iL_i
+2\sum_iE_i
+Z.$$
Every displayed term is nonnegative. Hence
$$\Delta\ge0,
\qquad
|T|+|M|\le\frac{mn}{2}.$$
The even-start rail loss is already represented by  $2E_i$  in the whole charge. Charging it again as a separate donor would double count the same physical deficit. The revised non-reuse statement is therefore correct.5. Extraction failure remains distinct from grid-target failureThe concrete example
$$w=6,\quad h=4,\quad a=1,\quad\ell=2$$
has:
$$|H|=22,\qquad |M_H|=11,\qquad \rho_H=1.$$
The rail is odd-start, so its contribution is zero. Adding the feasible selection  $(2,2)$  makes the old capped donor have deficit exactly one.The old elbow  $H_0$  is a proper connected frozen subset of the enlarged positive component. No sequence of singles or mixed bundles can remove the rail endpoints and isolate  $H_0$ . This is a valid counterexample to the proposed general extraction rule.It is not a counterexample to the grid inequality. The owned donor pays the one unit exactly once, and the corrected whole-receiver ledger remains nonnegative.The written mathematics of the revised note therefore merits a terminal ACCEPT.
